title: Co-location with the volume conjecture and significance for the depth correspondence's period witnesses
html:
Co-location with the Volume Conjecture

The Kashaev–Murakami–Murakami volume conjecture (conj:kashaev-volume-conjecture) sets q = e^{2\pi i / N} for N \to \infty. Here q runs over primitive N-th roots of unity. As N grows past n, q enters the failure locus \mathrm{NonBaer}(H_n(q)):

  • For N = 2k with k \leq n: q = \zeta_{2k} sits in the failure locus. Baer-* fails, Wedderburn fails, and the asymptotic-N regime activates.
  • For N \gg n: q = \zeta_N may fall outside the failure locus for H_n(q) at fixed n. However, as N \to \infty, the relevant Hecke order n grows with the colored-Jones level, eventually entering the failure locus.

Therefore, the Volume Conjecture's archimedean asymptotic regime exactly traces the trajectory through the Baer--failure locus. The loss of Baer- projection-generation supplies the structural mechanism of the wall-crossing transition.

This co-location is the Hecke-algebra face of the phenomenon that forces hyperbolic 3-manifold volumes to appear at depth 2 in the period filtration. The radical at the failure locus produces the period-class-non-trivial elements upon archimedean specialisation. See rem:vc-as-depth-2-instance for the depth-2 reading.

Significance for the depth correspondence

Combined with conj:gb-depth-period-correspondence, the projections \{e_\lambda\} become explicit witnesses for Goncharov period classes. Under \tau_{\mathrm{arch}}, e_{\lambda_K} \cdot \mathrm{Li}_2^q(z_K) generates the period class [\mathrm{Vol}(K)] \in \mathcal{P}_2 / \mathcal{P}_1 for any hyperbolic knot K with dominant cell \lambda_K and shape parameter z_K. The figure-8 instance evaluates as e_{(2,2)} \cdot \mathrm{Li}_2^q(\zeta_6).
